source.description:
## Problem

Fresh Pi requests carry substantial context before any conversation exists. A local `before_provider_request` capture (terminated before network transmission) measured:

- Minimal Pi without discovered extensions/skills/context: 5.7 KB payload (~1.4K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~`: 78.5 KB (~20K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~/dev/xtmux`: 82.2 KB (~21K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~/dev/core`: 127.2 KB (~32K tokens)

Nano-GPT first requests around 50K tokens are therefore plausible once an explicitly invoked skill body is added. For example, `multiplexing/SKILL.md` is 46.8 KB, `planning/SKILL.md` is 24.3 KB, and `using-specialists/SKILL.md` is 21.7 KB.

## Root cause

`packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts` eagerly appends project intelligence to every provider request. It currently injects:

- the complete first matching roadmap/architecture file (`ROADMAP.md` is 19.7 KB in core),
- every `.claude/rules/**/*.md` body,
- a recursive inventory of every Markdown file under `.claude/skills`, including references/docs rather than only skill entrypoints,
- `.xtrm/memory.md`, and
- the complete `using-xtrm` skill body.

In the core capture, the `Project Intelligence Context` section alone was ~34.9 KB. The recursive project-skill inventory also duplicates Pi’s built-in `<available_skills>` catalog, which already contributed ~35 KB for 59 skill metadata entries. Thirty tool schemas contributed another ~24.6 KB.

This is independent of the separate long-session problem where repeated tool rounds replay 200K-370K contexts.

## Desired direction

Make xtrm-loader routing-oriented instead of eagerly embedding whole documentation trees. Prefer concise paths/summaries and on-demand reads. Preserve genuinely essential session memory and operating constraints, but remove duplicate skill discovery and full roadmap/rules payloads from every turn.

## Verification notes

Use a temporary explicit extension with `before_provider_request` to capture the exact serialized payload and terminate before network transmission. Compare payload bytes and section composition before/after; provider-reported first-turn input tokens remain the final truth when running a controlled live smoke.

source.description:
## Problem

`bd prime` currently dumps 265 KB of Persistent Memories on every SessionStart hook fire (98.7% of its 269 KB total output). The 555-memory backlog has never been synthesized in this repo; many entries are stale (superseded by later work), redundant (multiple bearings of the same fact), or contradicted (later memory disagrees with earlier one).

## Task

Run the full memory-processor workflow (via `memory-audit-transaction` skill) with an AGGRESSIVE pruning stance:

- When a memory is even PLAUSIBLY stale/redundant/contradicted, classify accordingly instead of Current.
- Skip only when genuinely unverifiable (per skill's Phase 6 conservative rule) — but do not use Skip as a hedge to keep dubious entries alive.
- Target reduction: 555 → ~50-80 Current entries in `.xtrm/memory.md` (aim for a lean, dense session-start context).

## Constraints (from memory-processor spec)

- Chunks of 20-30 memories per turn; decisions appended to `.tmp/memory-audit/decisions.jsonl`.
- Phase 6 completeness gate is non-negotiable: `wc -l .tmp/memory-audit/keys.txt` == `wc -l .tmp/memory-audit/decisions.jsonl`.
- Phase 7 atomic hash-guarded prune; per-key backups in `.tmp/memory-audit/backup/`.
- Phase 8 writes filtered Current rows to `.xtrm/memory.md`.
- No destructive git.

## Model + launch

- `--model nano-gpt/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` (1M context — needed for the 555-memory input).
- Detached tmux session for background run.

## Success criteria

- `.xtrm/memory.md` populated (was 939-byte bootstrap placeholder).
- `bd stats` shows meaningfully fewer memories (target: 50-80).
- Next-session `bd prime` output measurably smaller (target: < 50 KB total, < 45 KB memories).
- Final report in bead notes: counts (Current / Stale / Contradicted / Redundant / Skipped) + measured reduction.

## Related

- xtrm-x12p3 (parent) — xtrm-loader eager-load reduction, this closes the memory-side of the same problem.
- Follow-up if reduction is insufficient: file a bead to strip `bd prime` from SessionStart entirely (keep only on-demand agent invocation).
source.title: memory-processor: aggressive prune of 555 stale/redundant memories
